title: Stack settings remove repeated context allocation; tasks carry an inline copy
scope: Intermediate stack-copy implementation, not the later packed-header or owned-callback changes. All six ordinary allocation tests passed; complete Windows jobs failed in separate C fixture compilation. Not acceptance of the current branch.
comparison: Each fwp service scope versus a plain fwp state update at matching 1/32/128 calls, O2, collection disabled. The saved 64-byte request versus the earlier Linux AMD64 baseline applies to gzip and deadline calls. No elapsed-time or C/Rust comparison.
limits: Managed allocation requests, requested bytes, and final charged storage only; not peak/process memory. Raw buffers, allocator metadata and pages are excluded. Plain programs omit the service-owner fields; their task sizes are not the old service task size. The old service task was 1512 bytes on Linux AMD64; this revision measures 1576, a 64-byte increase.

binary_observations.scope: Existing instrumented O2 binaries; not uninstrumented performance or a whole-stack bound.

linux_amd64.context_copy: Four movups 16-byte loads at 0xb520..0xb52b and movaps stores to stack at 0xb52f..0xb53e; the context reserves 64 stack bytes at 0xb4e5.
linux_amd64.task_allocation: Only lazy root-task creation allocates in this function: size 0x628 (1576) at 0xb580/0xb5e3, published as fwp_root at 0xb626. The per-call 64-byte scope allocation in the old baseline is absent.

macos_arm64.context_copy: Two paired 128-bit loads at 0x100008e74/0x100008e78 and paired stores at 0x100008e7c/0x100008e80 copy 64 bytes to the stack.
macos_arm64.task_allocation: Lazy root-task allocation requests 608 bytes at 0x100008e24; ordinary repeated scope calls skip it.
